flawed_step: Lines 0627–0635 claim that every nondegenerate quadratic space of dimension 2n over a finite field decomposes into n hyperbolic pairs. This false claim is invoked at line 0697.
counterexample: Take n=1, V=F_3^2, and Q(x,y)=x^2+y^2. Its associated bilinear form is B((x,y),(x',y'))=2xx'+2yy', whose matrix diag(2,2) has determinant 1 in F_3, so B is nondegenerate. But the only squares in F_3 are 0 and 1, so x^2+y^2=0 implies x=y=0. Thus V has no nonzero singular vector and hence no hyperbolic pair, contradicting the stated fact.
assessment_summary: The asserted quadratic-form decomposition requires a split (maximal Witt-index) hypothesis, which is absent. Since the later proof explicitly cites this false fact, the proof is invalid as written.
